description: Cryptographic receipts for machine-checked decisions against the compiled autonomous-agent provisions of Section 7. Each check was evaluated by ICME Preflight (https://docs.icme.io): a local SMT solver and an independent cloud automated-reasoning engine both evaluate the action; either engine returning UNSAT blocks it. Every check produces a zero-knowledge proof that can be independently verified (single-use) without re-running the solvers. Proofs are left unconsumed so the Firm can verify them independently via POST /v1/verifyProof.
compiled_from: Section 7, sentences 1 and 3, plus the Section 2 definition of Sensitive Information (all verbatim) of the FRB Generative AI Policy, Version 2.0, effective June 18, 2026

notes: Proofs are single-use for verification and have been left unconsumed so the Firm can verify them independently via POST /v1/verifyProof.

At publication, the zero-knowledge proof for the blocked consent decision (proof 672c0020...) is confirmed generated and valid. The remaining proof IDs were issued at check time but their proofs were still generating; they can be retrieved via GET /v1/proof/{id} once complete.

Natural-language fact extraction proved sensitive to phrasing: negated or implicit facts were sometimes dropped unless stated explicitly, and several checks required rephrasing before both verification engines agreed. Production integrations should assert facts as structured values from authoritative systems rather than narrating them.
